basis: Manually cross-checked recovered Ghidra pseudocode against the pinned stock Assembly export for the cited functions and raw state offsets.
Used MP4 relocation evidence for the static misc_device object identity and MP5 callsite inventory for resource-surface coverage.
Only exact pointer identity, static object identity, raw offsets, and callsite arguments are promoted; lifecycle completeness and semantic ownership remain separate questions.

evidence.claim: The value returned by devm_kmalloc is stored at the raw client offset +0xb8 and the same local pointer is passed to vibrator_init, haptic_init, and ram_work_init.
aw_remove loads a pointer from the same raw client offset +0xb8 before issuing teardown calls.
Stock AArch64 assembly corroborates allocation result storage at the same raw offset.

limits: The recovered pointer identity is strong, but this review does not assign a complete C type or field-name layout to the containing object.
This relation alone does not establish that every probe failure path reaches the same teardown operations.

evidence.claim: The .data relocation identifies richtap_misc and its pointer to left_fops.
Probe calls misc_register(richtap_misc).
Remove calls misc_deregister(richtap_misc) using the same static object.

limits: The return from misc_register is not checked in the recovered probe pseudocode.
This confirms object identity and calls, not successful registration on every path or complete file-operation quiescence.

evidence.claim: vibrator_init calls hrtimer_init(state+0x330) and stores vibrator_timer_func at raw state offset +0x358.
Stock Assembly confirms the call and raw callback-pointer store.
Remove calls hrtimer_cancel(state+0x330) after recovering the shared state pointer.
Stock Assembly passes x19+0x330 to hrtimer_cancel.

limits: A raw offset correspondence does not recover the complete hrtimer field type or callback behavior.
The callback's ability to rearm work/timers and all concurrent access paths remain unreviewed.

evidence.claim: haptic_init calls hrtimer_init(state+0x520) and stores audio_timer_func at raw state offset +0x548.
Stock Assembly confirms the call and raw callback-pointer store.
Remove calls hrtimer_cancel(state+0x520) for the recovered same state base.
Stock Assembly passes x19+0x520 to hrtimer_cancel.

limits: A raw offset correspondence does not recover the complete hrtimer field type or callback behavior.
The callback's ability to rearm work/timers and all concurrent access paths remain unreviewed.

evidence.claim: ram_work_init initializes raw object offset +0x3c0, stores ram_work_routine at +0x3d8, initializes the timer subobject at +0x3e0, and queues +0x3c0.
Stock Assembly confirms distinct raw offsets for the timer subobject and queued delayed-work object.
Remove calls cancel_delayed_work_sync(state+0x3c0) on the recovered same state base.
Stock Assembly passes x19+0x3c0 to cancel_delayed_work_sync.

limits: The stored ram_work_routine pointer is kept distinct from delayed_work_timer_fn, which is supplied to init_timer_key.
This relation does not establish asynchronous firmware callback quiescence or prove all producers are stopped before remove.

evidence.claim: irq_config passes its state pointer as dev_id to devm_request_threaded_irq and names irq_handle as the threaded handler.
Stock Assembly corroborates the same state pointer argument.
Remove derives the interrupt from the state GPIO slot and passes the same recovered state pointer to devm_free_irq.

limits: irq_config may skip registration for some state conditions; its error paths and the two devm_free_irq callsites are not fully path-paired here.
The callback ABI and synchronization relative to firmware, work, and user mappings remain open.

resource_group_review.evidence: MP5 records one alloc_workqueue call and no direct destroy_workqueue import/reference; probe stores the returned pointer at state+0x448. aw_remove has no identified destroy_workqueue call.
resource_group_review.limits: This is an unresolved release/lifetime question, not a leak conclusion. queue_work_on targets and the custom workqueue argument still need per-call dataflow.

resource_group_review.evidence: MP5 records two get_free_pages_noprof callsites and one free_pages callsite; aw_remove frees the pointer loaded from state+0x610.
resource_group_review.limits: The two acquisition sites, success/error paths, and the state+0x610 owner have not been joined into a complete path proof.

resource_group_review.evidence: MP5 inventories devm_kmalloc, __kmalloc_noprof, __kmalloc_large_noprof, devm_kfree, and kfree references.
resource_group_review.limits: Counts do not prove which allocation each free consumes or whether all error paths are balanced.

resource_group_review.evidence: MP5 inventories devm_gpio_request_one and gpio_free at different counts.
resource_group_review.limits: GPIO identities, request outcomes, devres semantics, and path conditions are not paired.

resource_group_review.evidence: The registration argument and remove dev_id match the shared state pointer; MP5 has one registration and two explicit devm_free_irq callsites.
resource_group_review.limits: Failure-unwind pairing and registration-skip conditions remain open.

resource_group_review.evidence: misc_register and misc_deregister both reference richtap_misc; MP4 relocations bind that object to left_fops.
resource_group_review.limits: Registration result handling and open-file lifetime relative to remove are not proven.

resource_group_review.evidence: MP5 records two sysfs_create_group calls and no direct sysfs_remove_group reference.
resource_group_review.limits: No cleanup conclusion is made until ownership through the exact target kernel APIs and object lifetime is traced.

resource_group_review.evidence: MP5 records devm_led_classdev_register_ext and no explicit unregister import.
resource_group_review.limits: Managed cleanup behavior and its device-lifetime boundary remain unverified.

resource_group_review.evidence: vibrator_init state+0x330 pairs with aw_remove cancel at +0x330; haptic_init state+0x520 pairs with aw_remove cancel at +0x520. MP5 also contains three other start calls and additional cancel references.
resource_group_review.limits: All callback rearm paths and full timer-to-work ownership remain open.

resource_group_review.evidence: MP4 confirms two request_firmware_nowait sites targeting ram_load; MP5 inventories synchronous and asynchronous request/release references.
resource_group_review.limits: Outstanding callback completion and object lifetime during remove are not joined.

resource_group_review.evidence: MP5 records three cpu_latency_qos_add_request and three remove references.
resource_group_review.limits: Request object identity and conditional path pairing are not reviewed.

open_blockers: Trace pointer origins and concrete target sets for the other 154 CALLIND sites; keep the three computed-target hypotheses unpromoted.
Trace the stored alloc_workqueue pointer and prove its release, consumers, and teardown ordering.
Join both page allocation sites and all relevant heap/GPIO/IRQ/latency-QoS resources by pointer identity and success/error path.
Resolve misc/open file and mmap lifetime against teardown; static register/deregister object identity is not a complete ABI/lifetime proof.
Resolve sysfs and devm LED lifetime using the exact target-kernel sources and registrations.
Prove asynchronous firmware callbacks and every work/timer producer are quiesced before state memory can be released.
Candidate source, candidate Joern analysis, candidate Docker build, relational oracle, and independent review remain unstarted.
